lines: It held when I needed it. That matters more than how it looks.
The damage is honest. This piece did its work.
I took a hit that would have ended worse without it.
It earned its scratches out there.
I was glad to have it when the fighting reached me.
The fastening stayed secure even while I was running.
It gave me enough protection to reach the door.
I tested it under conditions I would rather not repeat.
There is wear along the edge, but nothing failed.
It turned a dangerous moment into a survivable one.
I trusted it because trouble gave me no time to hesitate.
The fit needs adjusting after what it went through.
I heard the strike land and felt the gear take most of it.
It worked. I hope that remains its only field test.
This mark came from the fight, not poor storage.
I would recommend the same make after seeing it hold up.
It protected the parts of me required for reading and breathing.
The repair can wait until I record exactly where it wore down.
I came home with bruises instead of worse. Give it some credit.
Practical gear becomes very persuasive once arrows start moving.
It has not seen combat, and I would be pleased to keep it that way.
No field marks yet. Only dust from the shelf.
I checked the fit, but danger has not tested it.
It remains ready and entirely theoretical.
The straps are sound. I cannot tell you more without lying.
I have worn it for practice, never under attack.
Nothing has struck it harder than the corner of my desk.
It looks serviceable. That is not the same as proven.
I keep it close when the bell rings, though I have not needed it.
The condition is excellent because trouble passed me by.
I can report on the stitching, not its courage under fire.
It has spent more time beside the lectern than on my shoulders.
I would rather maintain unused gear than repair tested gear.
There are no battle scratches to interpret.
I prepared it before the last alarm, then stayed behind the door.
The buckles work in a quiet room. That is all I know.
It is ready if needed, but I will not invent a heroic account.
No enemy has given me reason to judge it yet.
I have kept it dry, fitted, and mercifully unused.
Ask me again after a fight, though I hope you never can.
